nodes.label: A manifest/tag version disagreement rejects the release and trusts neither side
nodes.norm_label: manifest/tag version disagreement rejects the release and trusts neither side
nodes.description: manifestAgreesWithTag() in apps/updater-worker-android/src/index.js compares the release’s own latest.json `version` against the version parsed from the android-v<versionName> tag. A string that differs in either direction is malformed and the release is skipped; an absent version cannot disagree, so the tag stays authoritative; a non-string version is malformed. Tested both orderings plus the desktop-compatibility-version case.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t10-android-updater-fail-closed [ses_f1da6ec9cffeT1MeCKOlQ1jSGQ].md:L4589] **Manifest/tag disagreement: reject the release, do not trust either side.** `version` always comes from the tag. If the release's `latest.json` has a string `version` that differs from the tag version (either direction), the release is malformed: it is skipped and discovery continues with the next older Android release; if none qualifies, the 404 unavailable response. An absent `version` cannot disagree, so the tag stays authoritative; a non-string `version` is malformed. `versionCode` comes from `platforms.android.versionCode` / `version_code` and must be a non-negative safe integer (or an all-digit string); anything else rejects the release rather than being coerced.

nodes.label: A short page is the only sound pagination stop rule
nodes.norm_label: a short page is the only sound pagination stop rule
nodes.description: The first implementation used "non-empty ⇒ keep paging", which cost an extra list call on every request against a small repository and consumed the queued tag-detail response in the positional fetch mock. Switching to len < RELEASES_PER_PAGE is semantically correct against real GitHub, keeps the happy path at three calls, and is what makes the page-3 fixture (two full 100-entry pages) meaningful.

nodes.label: Read the page size back out of the shared destination URL instead of hard-coding it
nodes.norm_label: read the page size back out of the shared destination url instead of hard-coding it
nodes.description: per_page is defined in destinations.js, which was outside the write allowlist for this task. Rather than duplicating the constant, RELEASES_PER_PAGE parses it back out of githubReleasesListUrl() with /[?&]per_page=(\d+)/ and falls back to 100. The two cannot drift, and the short-page stop rule then rests on the real request shape rather than a local assumption.

nodes.norm_label: malformed android versioncode is rejected rather than coerced

nodes.label: MAX_ANDROID_RELEASE_PAGES bounds the per-request fan-out and is exported for tests
nodes.norm_label: max_android_release_pages bounds the per-request fan-out and is exported for tests
nodes.description: The cap is 3, exported from index.js so a test can assert it is a small bounded integer rather than reading the literal back out of behaviour. It sits above the short-page rule as a second, independent stop: full pages all the way to the cap with no Android artifact ends in the 404 unavailable response, and no fourth call is made.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t10-android-updater-fail-closed [ses_f1da6ec9cffeT1MeCKOlQ1jSGQ].md:L4588] **Cap: `MAX_ANDROID_RELEASE_PAGES = 3`**, exported from `index.js` (documented in a block comment as the per-request fan-out bound). Paging stops at the first *short* page: GitHub only serves a further page when the current one came back full, so the page size is read back out of `githubReleasesListUrl()` (`RELEASES_PER_PAGE`) rather than hard-coded — this also keeps the common case at one discovery call. A release-list entry is a candidate only if it is a stable (non-draft, non-prerelease) `android-v<versionName>` tag; when the entry carries an `assets` array it must contain an `.apk`, otherwise paging continues.

nodes.label: A single positional mockResolvedValueOnce was consumed by all three fetchChannelReleases pagination requests, so the versions-route test hit real fetch and returned 502
nodes.norm_label: positional fetch mock outlived pagination
nodes.description: The Android worker tests queue fetch responses positionally. Adding a second list call for a non-empty page 1 meant the queued tag-detail response — a non-array — was consumed as page 2, the worker treated it as failure, and every test returned 404. A scratch script outside the repo was what surfaced it; the suite alone showed only 404s with no indication why.

nodes.norm_label: missing-export typeerror is not acceptable red proof

nodes.norm_label: the update-unavailable body carries no version string, and that is asserted
nodes.description: The failure shape is the worker’s existing jsonError verbatim: HTTP 404, text/plain; charset=utf-8, CORS-tagged, body "No Android release is available for this device. nodes.label: tgrep rejects an unescaped open paren that GNU grep treats as literal
nodes.norm_label: tgrep rejects an unescaped open paren that gnu grep treats as literal
nodes.description: `grep -n '^  it('` — listing every it() in a test file — failed with "regex parse error" and "unclosed group; PCRE-style fallback failed: Parsing error at position 6: Opening parenthesis without closing parenthesis". GNU grep in BRE mode treats that paren as a literal and matches. The pattern has to be written `^  it\(` for tgrep, so a command copied from a GNU habit does not silently return nothing: it errors, which is at least visible.
